 Hon'Ble Vikram D. Chauhan, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for applicant and learned Aga for the State.

2. The present application has been filed for quashing the entire proceedings of Criminal Case
No.855 of 2011 (Old Case No.53 of 2001) (State Vs. Gulam Mohammad) based on undated
application moved by opposite party no.2 (vide order dated 8.1.2001 by C.J.M.) as well as
cognizance order dated 8.1.2001 under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954
(Pfa Act), Police Station Chakia, District Chandauli as well as consequential orders including
execution of order dated 3.9.2025 issuing N.B.W. against applicant pending before the Civil Judge
(Junior Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Chakia, Chandauli.

entities.text:
Civil Judge
(Junior Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Chakia, Chandauli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3.  It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that cognizance order dated 8.1.2001 is not tenable as neither the First Information Report has been lodged nor the complaint.

However,
learned counsel for applicant admits that in the year 2001 applicant was enlarged on bail and upto 2020 applicant has appeared before the court concerned, thereafter, he could not appear before the court concerned and as such, non bailable warrant has been issued against him.
4. Insofar as putting challenge to the summoning order, the summoning order is of the year 2001.
The challenge to the summoning order at such later stage cannot be permitted as the same would delay the trial.
No explanation has been offered by learned counsel for applicant as to why in the year 2001 itself summoning order was not put to challenge when the applicant was enlarged on bail.
Applicant is trying to delay the disposal of criminal case.
Applicant has all the opportunity to raise their objection with regard to tenability of proceedings.
Conduct of applicant challenging the summoning order before this Court after more than 24 years is glaring example of abuse of process of law.
5. Insofar as non bailable warrant issued against applicant is concerned, from perusal of the order sheet would go to show that applicant is absent from the trial since October, 2023.
Learned counsel for applicant admits that applicant was earlier enlarged on bail and bail is being granted to accused so that he may participate in trial court proceedings.
Applicant after being enlarged on bail is not entitled to choose his own ways to appear before the court concerned at his own leisure.
The petition lacks merit.
6. Accordingly, the application under Section 528 BNSS is dismissed.
7. The trial court is directed to proceed with the case and decide the same within a period of six months.
In case non bailable warrant issued, all the authorities shall co-operate in execution of non bailable warrant without fail.
(Vikram D. Chauhan,J.) October 29, 2025 D. Tamang
